subject: RE: Finex throughput sizing — post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Finex throughput sizing — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great call. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size throughput and confirm SLOs for the pilot.

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary workload: clinical-document summarization (user uploads long visit notes, model returns a structured summary).
- Expected steady-state: ~40 requests/sec (QPS) during business hours.
- Peak bursts: up to 120 QPS for short windows (~5–10 minutes) driven by batch uploads.
- Average tokens per request (input + output): ~1,200 tokens.
- Latency requirement: 95th <= 800ms for streaming responses to keep UI snappy.
- Concurrency: expected 250 concurrent user sessions at peak.
- Model preference: open-model family (LLaMA-3-ish), but open to recommendations for quantized variants.

Immediate asks for sizing: can you confirm the steady vs peak QPS numbers above and the average tokens per request? Also let us know if streaming is required for the initial pilot (we've logged streaming as preferred).

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a quick spreadsheet or sample traffic profile (QPS vs time, tokens distribution).
2) We run a focused sizing exercise + cost estimate using those numbers, including options for batching, KV caching, and a streaming vs non-streaming baseline.
3) Schedule a 30‑minute follow-up next week to review results.

Attachment: I’ll include a small template for traffic (we can fill together) — Rafael will push our initial sizing based on the numbers you confirm.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Finex throughput sizing — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming the numbers from our end with a few clarifications:

- Steady-state: ~35–45 QPS (flattened over 8 hours).
- Peak: 100–130 QPS for 5–12 minute bursts (monthly cadence when clinics run batch exports).
- Tokens/request: we've measured 950–1,500 tokens depending on length; median ~1,150.
- Concurrency: we see ~200 concurrent active sessions typically, but allocate for 300 for headroom.
- Streaming: yes — preferred. The UI relies on a streaming response to progressively render sections of the summary.

I've attached our small traffic sample and a column showing historical burst windows. Also included is a target 95th latency goal of 800ms (client requirement).

Attachment: finex-throughput-v1.xlsx

Let us know if you need more detail (we can export request-level logs). Happy to take the sizing spreadsheet you mentioned.

—Alex
Alex Carter
VP Product — Finex Health
alex.carter@finexhealth.com | (650) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Alex Carter <alex.carter@finexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Finex throughput sizing — post-call follow-up

Hi all — looping in my sizing notes after I reviewed the attachment. High-level thoughts:

- With median tokens ~1,150 and steady 40 QPS, that maps to ~46k tokens/sec steady-state. Peak at 120 QPS -> ~138k tokens/sec.
- For streaming with 95th <= 800ms, we should assume low-latency model variants (int8/4-bit quant) and allocate for smaller micro-batching to preserve tail latency.
- Concurrency (300) implies we should size for both token throughput and connection count; recommend a pool of GPUs that supports concurrent KV cache active sessions.

Proposed quick experiment (week-of-3/8):
1) Redwood runs 3 load profiles against a candidate model variant (quantized) with your sample payloads: steady (40 QPS), burst (120 QPS), and mixed diurnal.
2) We'll capture tokens/sec, per-token latency, and 95/99 latency percentiles for streaming chunks.
3) Deliverable: a recommended capacity plan (GPU count, expected cost), plus tuning guidance (batching window, cache strategy).

Can we schedule a 30-min sync on 3/09 or 3/10 to confirm scope and kick off the experiments? Rafael — happy for you to propose a time.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Finex throughput sizing — post-call follow-up

Alex / Samir — perfect, thanks for the confirmation and the attachment.

I’ll coordinate the experiment and run three profiles as Marissa outlined. Action items:
- Rafael / Marissa: we’ll prepare the load harness and a preliminary costed capacity plan by 3/06.
- Finex: please confirm whether you can provide a small set of anonymized request traces (preferred) or whether we should use the sample payloads in finex-throughput-v1.xlsx. Traces will give better token-distribution accuracy.
- Confirm follow-up: 30 min on 2026-03-09 at 10:00 PT (proposed) — Alex, does this work?

Also: two quick clarifications for sizing accuracy:
1) Is the 95th 800ms target for end-to-end (client visible) or for strictly model server time? If end-to-end, we’ll need to budget ~150–250ms for network + UI rendering.
2) For streaming, please indicate minimal chunk size expectations (e.g., 64–128 tokens) so we can measure chunk-level latency.

Once I have confirmation on traces and the 95th definition we’ll lock the test matrix.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
